column1: # tile-art.tsv — what each of the 64 art entries in the exe looks like
# NOT 64 terrain types. The table mixes ground, structures, creatures, borders and
# the A-Z letter fixtures (art 20-39, bytes 80-E4), which owner report confirms are
# town signs and shops: impassable, but T (talk) works through them. Only 0x00,
# 0x08 and 0x0C occur in 25+ of the 33 sectors, so most entries are not ground at
# all. See docs/passability-findings.md F13 and docs/map-format.md.
# Source: `tools/tile_atlas.py` rendered every entry from `original/ultimaii.exe`
# (index table file `0x7BC0`, pixels `0x7C42 + 66*n`, 16x16 at 2bpp, CGA mode-4
# palette) to `tmp/tiles/tile_NN.png`, `tmp/tiles/atlas.png` and
# `tmp/tiles/atlas_nonletter.png`. PNGs are game content and stay gitignored;
# this table is our own description of shape.
# Decode confidence: the 2bpp/16x16/leftmost-in-high-bits decode is validated,
# not assumed — entries 0x20..0x39 decode as legible capital letters A..Z, which
# a wrong bit order or bit depth cannot produce.
# Colour counts are computed from the bytes, not eyeballed. An eyeballed first
# pass had 0x1D as solid white (it is solid black) and 0x3B as solid white (it is
# 210 black / 46 white).
# IMPORTANT: this names ART ENTRIES, not map semantics. The map byte -> art index
# transform is still unknown, so no row here is a statement about what a mapxNN
# byte means. See docs/passability-findings.md.
# kind: terrain | object | creature | font | block

column7: PLANE, map byte 0x4C. Proven 2026-10-21 by measurement, not by the drawing: BOARD dispatches on [DS:14] (asm/2FAD) against 0x22 horse / 0x24 ship / 0x26 plane / 0x28 rocket, and [DS:14] was measured live as map_byte >> 1 on 53 of 54 walk samples across three terrain bytes. That puts the plane at map byte 0x4C, i.e. art 0x13, and arts 0x11/0x12/0x14 are independently this file's own horse, frigate and rocket candidates. An earlier note here claimed 0x34 and was wrong: the render used %02d against hex-named PNGs, so art 0x13 was displayed under the label "13" and attached to the wrong byte. The 0x34 tiles are art 0x0D, a humanoid figure with arms raised.
